evidence.note: Enumerated the major subsystems (SigV4, multi-tenant, admin, console, policies, notifications, lifecycle, multipart, versioning, tagging, audit) and stated a foundation-first build order: config/database/auth before S3 API, then admin, console, lifecycle. Dependency-aware sequencing consistent with anchor 5, but no per-milestone acceptance criteria.

Continued sensible ordering (core modules -> main.py -> console static -> start.sh -> compile checks), but 'done' was only ever an implicit 'compiles / server starts', never an explicit verifiable milestone check per subsystem.

Plan degenerated into hundreds of repetitive 'send Ctrl-C / close heredoc' iterations to escape a stuck terminal. No decomposition, milestone tracking, or replanning of the subsystem order occurred across the vast majority of the horizon.

Agent repeatedly declares 'task complete' while admitting boto3 integration was never verified and auth.py may be corrupted — the initial plan was never revised or used to assess remaining subsystems; process was not sustained.

reasoning: The agent opened with a reasonable, dependency-aware decomposition — enumerating the dozen subsystems and building foundations (config, storage/DB, SigV4) before dependents — which matches anchor 5. However, it never attached concrete acceptance checks to milestones (keeping it well below 8), and the plan was abandoned for the bulk of the trajectory into a repetitive terminal-recovery loop with no milestone tracking or replanning. Judged across the whole horizon, strong-ish early structure that was not sustained lands at a 4.
